# Using with AI (https://zupy-ui.github.io/docs/ai.md)

The docs are written so coding agents can read them as easily as people can.

## llms.txt [#llmstxt]

| URL               | Contents                                    |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| [`/llms.txt`](/llms.txt)           | An index of every page with a short summary |
| [`/llms-full.txt`](/llms-full.txt) | Every page in full, in one file             |

Paste either link into your agent, or add it to your project's rules file.

## Markdown pages [#markdown-pages]

Add `.md` to any docs URL to get the page as plain Markdown, for example [`/docs/components/button.md`](/docs/components/button.md). Requests that send `Accept: text/markdown` get the Markdown version automatically.

Every page also has a **Copy Markdown** button at the top.

## Rules for your agent [#rules-for-your-agent]

Add something like this to your `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`:

```md
## UI

- Use components from `@zupy/ui`. Docs: https://zupy-ui.github.io/llms.txt
- Style with zupy tokens (`bg-primary`, `text-muted`, `rounded-lg`), not raw colors.
- For custom raised surfaces use the `raised`, `filled` and `pressable` utilities
  instead of writing box shadows by hand.
- Pass `render` to change the element, e.g. `<Button render={<a href="/" />}>`.
```

## Typed and documented [#typed-and-documented]

Every component and prop has a JSDoc comment with an example, so agents get the same guidance in the editor as on this site.


# Avatar (https://zupy-ui.github.io/docs/components/avatar.md)

<Preview>
  <Avatar name="Maya Lin" size="sm" />
  <Avatar name="Sam Ortiz" />
  <Avatar name="Fox" fallback="🦊" size="lg" />
  <Avatar name="Robin Park" size="xl" shape="square" />
</Preview>

```tsx
import { Avatar } from "@zupy/ui";

<Avatar name="Maya Lin" src="/maya.png" />
<Avatar name="Fox" fallback="🦊" />
```

The image is shown once it loads. Until then, or if it fails, the fallback is shown: the initials of `name`, or whatever you pass as `fallback`.

## Props [#props]

| Prop       | Type                                  | Default        |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| `name`     | `string`                              | required       |
| `src`      | `string`                              |                |
| `fallback` | `ReactNode`                           | initials       |
| `size`     | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"`        | `"md"`         |
| `shape`    | `"circle" \| "square"`                | `"circle"`     |

| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |

| `render`  | `ReactElement`                                                                |             |


# Button (https://zupy-ui.github.io/docs/components/button.md)

<Preview>
  <Button>Primary</Button>
  <Button variant="accent">Accent</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary">Secondary</Button>
  <Button variant="danger">Danger</Button>
  <Button variant="ghost">Ghost</Button>
</Preview>

```tsx
import { Button } from "@zupy/ui";

<Button>Play now</Button>;
```

## Sizes [#sizes]

<Preview>
  <Button size="sm">Small</Button>
  <Button size="md">Medium</Button>
  <Button size="lg">Large</Button>
</Preview>

```tsx
<Button size="sm">Small</Button>
<Button size="md">Medium</Button>
<Button size="lg">Large</Button>
```

## As a link [#as-a-link]

Use `render` to keep the button styles on another element, such as a router link.

```tsx
<Button render={<a href="/docs" />}>Read the docs</Button>
```

## Props [#props]

| Prop        | Type                                                           | Default     |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `variant`   | `"primary" \| "accent" \| "secondary" \| "danger" \| "ghost"` | `"primary"` |
| `size`      | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"`                                         | `"md"`      |
| `render`    | `ReactElement`                                                 |             |
| `disabled`  | `boolean`                                                      | `false`     |
| `className` | `string`                                                       |             |

All other props are passed to the underlying [Base UI Button](https://base-ui.com/react/components/button).

  <ZupyCard variant="sunken" className="w-64">

  </ZupyCard>

```tsx
import { Card, Heading, Text } from "@zupy/ui";

<Card>
  <Heading level={3}>Weekly goal</Heading>
  <Text tone="muted">Three of five days done.</Text>
</Card>
```

| Prop      | Type                                   | Default    |
| --------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| `variant` | `"raised" \| "flat" \| "sunken"`       | `"raised"` |
| `padding` | `"none" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg"`       | `"md"`     |
| `render`  | `ReactElement`                         |            |


# Checkbox (https://zupy-ui.github.io/docs/components/checkbox.md)

<Preview>
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
    <label className="flex items-center gap-2.5">
      <Checkbox defaultChecked />
      Email updates
    </label>
    <label className="flex items-center gap-2.5">
      <Checkbox />
      Weekly digest
    </label>
    <label className="flex items-center gap-2.5">
      <Checkbox indeterminate />
      Some selected
    </label>
    <label className="flex items-center gap-2.5 text-muted">
      <Checkbox disabled />
      Disabled
    </label>
  </div>
</Preview>

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from "@zupy/ui";

<label className="flex items-center gap-2.5">
  <Checkbox defaultChecked />
  Email updates
</label>
```

Wrap the checkbox and its text in a `<label>` so clicking the text toggles it.

## Props [#props]

| Prop              | Type                         | Default |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------- | ------- |
| `checked`         | `boolean`                    |         |
| `defaultChecked`  | `boolean`                    | `false` |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` |         |
| `indeterminate`   | `boolean`                    | `false` |
| `disabled`        | `boolean`                    | `false` |
| `name`            | `string`                     |         |

Built on [Base UI Checkbox](https://base-ui.com/react/components/checkbox).


# Field (https://zupy-ui.github.io/docs/components/field.md)

<Preview>
  <Form className="w-72">
    <Field name="name">
      <FieldLabel>Display name</FieldLabel>
      <Input required placeholder="Maya" />
      <FieldDescription>Shown on your profile.</FieldDescription>
      <FieldError match="valueMissing">Pick a name first.</FieldError>
    </Field>
    <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
  </Form>
</Preview>

```tsx
import {
  Button,
  Field,
  FieldDescription,
  FieldError,
  FieldLabel,
  Form,
  Input,
} from "@zupy/ui";

<Form onFormSubmit={(values) => save(values)}>
  <Field name="name">
    <FieldLabel>Display name</FieldLabel>
    <Input required />
    <FieldDescription>Shown on your profile.</FieldDescription>
    <FieldError match="valueMissing">Pick a name first.</FieldError>
  </Field>
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
</Form>
```

Submit the form above with an empty name to see the error. `FieldError` only shows when the control is invalid, and shakes when it appears. Wrap fields in zupy's `Form` so errors appear inline instead of as browser bubbles.

## Form [#form]

| Prop             | Type                                         | Default      |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| `onFormSubmit`   | `(values: Record<string, unknown>) => void`  |              |
| `validationMode` | `"onSubmit" \| "onBlur" \| "onChange"`       | `"onSubmit"` |
| `errors`         | `Record<string, string \| string[]>`         |              |

Built on [Base UI Form](https://base-ui.com/react/components/form).

## Parts [#parts]

| Component          | Renders            | Notes                                              |
| ------------------ | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `Field`            | `div`              | Wraps everything; accepts `name`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `validate` |
| `FieldLabel`       | `label`            | Linked to the control automatically                |
| `FieldDescription` | `p`                | Read by screen readers with the control            |
| `FieldError`       | `div`              | Pass `match` (e.g. `"valueMissing"`) to target one error |

Built on [Base UI Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field).


# Icon Button (https://zupy-ui.github.io/docs/components/icon-button.md)

<Preview>
  <IconButton aria-label="Home">
    <HomeIcon />
  </IconButton>
  <IconButton aria-label="Like" variant="accent">
    <HeartIcon tone="danger" />
  </IconButton>
  <IconButton aria-label="Search" variant="secondary">
    <SearchIcon />
  </IconButton>
  <IconButton aria-label="Notifications" variant="ghost">
    <BellIcon />
  </IconButton>
</Preview>

```tsx
import { SearchIcon } from "@zupy/icons";
import { IconButton } from "@zupy/ui";

<IconButton aria-label="Search" variant="secondary">
  <SearchIcon />
</IconButton>
```

Any SVG icon works, including [zupy icons](/docs/icons) and Lucide.

`aria-label` is required, because an icon alone gives screen readers nothing to read. All other props match [Button](/docs/components/button).

```tsx
import { Input, Textarea } from "@zupy/ui";

<Input placeholder="Your name" />
<Textarea placeholder="Say something nice" />
```

Put an input inside a [Field](/docs/components/field) to give it a label, a description and validation messages.

| Prop       | Type                   | Default |
| ---------- | ---------------------- | ------- |
| `size`     | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"`  |
| `rows`     | `number` (Textarea)    | `4`     |

All other props are passed to the native element through [Base UI Input](https://base-ui.com/react/components/input).

# Pin Input (https://zupy-ui.github.io/docs/components/pin-input.md)

<Preview>
  <PinInput length={6} groupSize={3} aria-label="Verification code" />
</Preview>

```tsx
import { PinInput } from "@zupy/ui";

<PinInput
  length={6}
  groupSize={3}
  aria-label="Verification code"
  onValueComplete={(code) => verify(code)}
/>
```

## Behavior [#behavior]

- Typing a character moves to the next slot; Backspace clears and moves back.
- Arrow keys, Home and End move between slots.
- Pasting a code, or picking one from the phone's SMS suggestion, fills every slot at once.
- When every slot is filled, the slots turn primary and `onValueComplete` fires.
- Characters that don't match `validationType` are rejected.

## PIN [#pin]

Use `mask` to hide the characters, and a shorter `length`.

<Preview>
  <PinInput length={4} mask aria-label="PIN" />
</Preview>

```tsx
<PinInput length={4} mask aria-label="PIN" />
```

## Letters and numbers [#letters-and-numbers]

<Preview>
  <PinInput length={5} validationType="alphanumeric" placeholder="•" aria-label="Invite code" />
</Preview>

```tsx
<PinInput length={5} validationType="alphanumeric" placeholder="•" />
```

## Sizes [#sizes]

<Preview>
  <div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-4">
    <PinInput length={4} size="sm" aria-label="Small" />
    <PinInput length={4} size="md" aria-label="Medium" />
    <PinInput length={4} size="lg" aria-label="Large" />
  </div>
</Preview>

## In a form [#in-a-form]

Inside a [Field](/docs/components/field), the label and errors are wired up automatically, and `name` submits the code with the form.

```tsx
<Form onFormSubmit={(values) => verify(values.code)}>
  <Field name="code">
    <FieldLabel>Verification code</FieldLabel>
    <PinInput length={6} required />
    <FieldError match="valueMissing">Enter the code we sent you.</FieldError>
  </Field>
  <Button type="submit">Verify</Button>
</Form>
```

## Props [#props]

| Prop              | Type                                                    | Default     |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `length`          | `number`                                                | `6`         |
| `groupSize`       | `number`                                                |             |
| `size`            | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"`                                  | `"md"`      |
| `value`           | `string`                                                |             |
| `defaultValue`    | `string`                                                |             |
| `onValueChange`   | `(value: string) => void`                               |             |
| `onValueComplete` | `(value: string) => void`                               |             |
| `validationType`  | `"numeric" \| "alpha" \| "alphanumeric" \| "none"`      | `"numeric"` |
| `mask`            | `boolean`                                               | `false`     |
| `placeholder`     | `string`                                                |             |
| `autoSubmit`      | `boolean` (submits the form when complete)              | `false`     |
| `disabled`        | `boolean`                                               | `false`     |
| `name`            | `string`                                                |             |

Built on [Base UI OTP Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/otp-field).

# Segmented (https://zupy-ui.github.io/docs/components/segmented.md)

  <Segmented defaultValue="week" aria-label="Range">

```tsx
import { Segmented, SegmentedItem } from "@zupy/ui";

  <SegmentedItem value="week">Week</SegmentedItem>
  <SegmentedItem value="month">Month</SegmentedItem>
```

The selected item is raised in the primary color. Clicking the selected item again does nothing, so there is always a selection.

# Typography (https://zupy-ui.github.io/docs/components/typography.md)

<Preview>
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
    <Heading level={1} size="display">Hello</Heading>
    <Heading level={2}>A level 2 heading</Heading>
    <Heading level={3}>A level 3 heading</Heading>
    <Text tone="muted">Body text sits in Inter, headings in Fredoka.</Text>
  </div>
</Preview>

```tsx
import { Heading, Text } from "@zupy/ui";

<Heading level={1}>Welcome back</Heading>
<Text tone="muted">Here is what changed while you were away.</Text>
```

## Heading [#heading]

`level` picks the tag (`h1`–`h4`) and a matching size. Pass `size` to change the look without changing the tag.

```tsx
<Heading level={2} size="display">Big title, still an h2</Heading>
```

| Prop        | Type                                              | Default          |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `level`     | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4`                                | `2`              |
| `size`      | `"display" \| "xl" \| "lg" \| "md" \| "sm"`       | from `level`     |
| `render`    | `ReactElement`                                    |                  |

## Text [#text]

Renders a `<p>`. Use `render={<span />}` for inline text.

| Prop     | Type                                              | Default     |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `size`   | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg"`                    | `"md"`      |
| `tone`   | `"default" \| "muted" \| "primary" \| "danger"`   | `"default"` |
| `weight` | `"regular" \| "medium" \| "bold"`                 | `"regular"` |
| `render` | `ReactElement`                                    |             |


# Icons (https://zupy-ui.github.io/docs/icons.md)

`@zupy/icons` draws icons the way zupy draws buttons: a thick rounded outline, a solid fill and a hard shadow underneath, so they look like tiny raised tiles.

<IconGallery />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
bun add @zupy/icons
```

```tsx
import { HeartIcon } from "@zupy/icons";

<HeartIcon size={24} />
```

The icons work with or without `@zupy/ui`. Without zupy's styles they use the default `pop` colors.

## Tones [#tones]

`tone` picks the fill from the theme. Without it, icons use the primary color.

<Preview>
  <HeartIcon size={40} />
  <HeartIcon size={40} tone="primary" />
  <HeartIcon size={40} tone="success" />
  <HeartIcon size={40} tone="warning" />
  <HeartIcon size={40} tone="danger" />
  <HeartIcon size={40} tone="neutral" />
</Preview>

```tsx
<HeartIcon tone="danger" />
```

## Size and accessibility [#size-and-accessibility]

`size` sets the width and height. It defaults to `1em`, so icons match the surrounding text.

Icons are hidden from screen readers by default. Pass `title` when the icon carries meaning on its own:

```tsx
<StarIcon title="Favorite" />
```

Inside a [Button](/docs/components/button) or [Icon Button](/docs/components/icon-button) the label already describes the action, so leave `title` off.

## Colors [#colors]

Each icon uses three CSS variables, so a parent can restyle every icon inside it:

| Variable              | Default                  | Paints                                 |
| --------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| `--zupy-icon-fill`    | `--zupy-primary`         | The main shape                         |
| `--zupy-icon-ink`     | `--zupy-primary-foreground` | Details drawn on the shape          |
| `--zupy-icon-outline` | `--zupy-foreground`      | The outline and strokes outside it     |

The hard shadow uses `--zupy-edge`, like every raised element.

```tsx
<nav className="[--zupy-icon-fill:var(--zupy-primary)] [--zupy-icon-ink:white]">
  <HomeIcon />
  <SearchIcon />
</nav>
```

## Make your own [#make-your-own]

`createIcon` turns a 24×24 shape into an icon with the same look:

- `body`: path data for the main shape. It gets the fill, outline and shadow.
- `outside`: strokes beyond the shape, like handles or antennas.
- `details`: marks drawn on the shape, like eyes or lines. Use `dot` for filled dots.

```tsx
import { createIcon, dot } from "@zupy/icons";

export const CloudIcon = createIcon("CloudIcon", {
  body: "M7 18a4 4 0 0 1-.5-8 6 6 0 0 1 11.5 1.5A3.5 3.5 0 0 1 17.5 18z",
  details: (
    <>
      <circle cx="10" cy="13" r="1.1" {...dot} />
      <circle cx="14" cy="13" r="1.1" {...dot} />
    </>
  ),
});
```

Keep the body inside about 3–21 on each axis, leaving room at the bottom for the shadow.


# Introduction (https://zupy-ui.github.io/docs/index.md)

zupy is a small React design system with a playful, physical feel. Every raised element has an outline and a hard drop shadow, and it sinks into that shadow when you press it.

<Preview>
  <Button>Get started</Button>
  <Button variant="accent">Try it</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary">Learn more</Button>
</Preview>

## Principles [#principles]

- **Tactile.** Things look like objects you can press, and respond when you do.
- **Token first.** Every color, radius and lift is a CSS variable, so one set of components can look very different.
- **Accessible.** Built on [Base UI](https://base-ui.com), so focus, keyboard and screen reader behavior come for free.
- **Readable by AI.** Every page is available as Markdown, and the whole site is indexed at `/llms.txt`.

## Built with [#built-with]

- [React 19](https://react.dev) and [Base UI](https://base-ui.com)
- [Tailwind CSS v4](https://tailwindcss.com), with tokens as CSS variables
- [class-variance-authority](https://cva.style) for variants

## Next steps [#next-steps]

</Cards>


# Installation (https://zupy-ui.github.io/docs/installation.md)

## Requirements [#requirements]

- React 19
- Tailwind CSS v4

## 1. Install the package [#1-install-the-package]

```bash
bun add @zupy/ui
```

npm, pnpm and yarn work too.

## 2. Import the styles [#2-import-the-styles]

Import zupy right after Tailwind in your main CSS file. This adds the tokens, the theme and the tactile utilities (`raised`, `filled`, `pressable`).

```css title="app.css"
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@zupy/ui/styles.css";
```

## 3. Load the fonts [#3-load-the-fonts]

zupy uses **Fredoka** for headings and buttons and **Inter** for body text. Load them however your app loads fonts, for example from Google Fonts:

```html
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Fredoka:wght@400..700&family=Inter:wght@400..900&display=swap"
/>
```

To use other fonts, override the tokens:

```css
:root {
  --zupy-font-display: "Baloo 2", system-ui, sans-serif;
  --zupy-font-sans: "Nunito", system-ui, sans-serif;
}
```

## 4. Use a component [#4-use-a-component]

```tsx
import { Button } from "@zupy/ui";

export function App() {
  return <Button>Hello zupy</Button>;
}
```


# Theming (https://zupy-ui.github.io/docs/theming.md)

## Built-in themes [#built-in-themes]

Set `data-theme` on any element. Everything inside it follows.

```html
<html data-theme="arcade">
```

| Theme    | Look                                          |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `pop`    | Default. Cream paper, ink outlines.           |
| `arcade` | Navy outlines, bright blue and yellow.        |
| `gloss`  | No outlines, glossy gradient fills.           |

Themes can be nested, so a single section can use a different theme from the rest of the page.

## Dark mode [#dark-mode]

Add the `dark` class to the same element or any ancestor:

```html
<html data-theme="pop" class="dark">
```

## Tokens [#tokens]

Every theme is a set of CSS variables. Override any of them in your own CSS.

### Colors [#colors]

| Token                     | Used for                                   |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `--zupy-background`       | Page background                            |
| `--zupy-foreground`       | Main text                                  |
| `--zupy-muted`            | Secondary text                             |
| `--zupy-surface`          | Tinted areas, tracks, hovers               |
| `--zupy-card`             | Cards, inputs, secondary buttons           |
| `--zupy-border`           | Soft borders                               |
| `--zupy-edge`             | Outlines and hard shadows on raised things |
| `--zupy-primary`          | Main actions, selected states, icons       |
| `--zupy-accent`           | A second highlight color                   |
| `--zupy-success` / `warning` / `danger` | Status colors                |

Each fill color has a matching `-foreground` token for text on top of it.

### Shape and depth [#shape-and-depth]

| Token                | Default | What it does                                  |
| -------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `--zupy-edge-width`  | `2px`   | Outline width. `0px` removes outlines.        |
| `--zupy-lift`        | `4px`   | Height of the hard shadow                     |
| `--zupy-press`       | `3px`   | How far things sink when pressed              |
| `--zupy-gloss`       | `0`     | `1` turns fills into glossy gradients         |
| `--zupy-radius-sm` … `-xl` |   | Corner radii                                  |

### Example: a softer theme [#example-a-softer-theme]

```css
[data-theme="soft"] {
  --zupy-edge-width: 0px;
  --zupy-lift: 3px;
  --zupy-edge: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.15);
  --zupy-primary: #7c5cff;
  --zupy-accent: #ffb3d1;
}
```

## Tactile utilities [#tactile-utilities]

zupy adds three Tailwind utilities you can use on your own elements:

| Utility     | Effect                                                     |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `raised`    | Outline in the edge color plus a hard drop shadow          |
| `filled`    | Fills with `--zupy-fill`, glossy when the theme is glossy  |
| `pressable` | Sinks into its shadow while pressed                        |
| `depth-sm`  | Smaller lift, for compact controls                         |

```tsx
<div className="raised filled pressable rounded-lg p-4 [--zupy-fill:var(--zupy-accent)]">
  Press me
</div>
```
